title: SIH26080 requirement coverage
rules: A row is IMPLEMENTED only if the capability exists, is reachable in the app, and is backed by hash-verified evidence.
A row with a material gap is PARTIAL and states the gap. A capability that does not exist yet is PLANNED, never IMPLEMENTED.
No number is typed into this file: every figure is a pointer into a hash-verified evidence file, resolved by the API at request time.

rows.requirement: Raw NWP rainfall forecast as the input being corrected
rows.summary: Historical NOAA GEFS rainfall (2019 reforecast track and 2023-2025 operational-archive track) is reconstructed to canonical 24-hour accumulation windows and used as the Raw baseline (M0).
rows.limitation: Archival, historical data only: nothing ingests a current forecast cycle. The source is NOAA GEFS, not an NCMRWF model.

rows.summary: Forecast-time detection of the active monsoon, break and low/depression states was fitted on the 2000-2011 reforecast control forecasts, selected under a frozen protocol and tested once on the sealed years 2014-2016 against objective labels (IMD core-zone rainfall spells; ERA5 850 hPa vorticity). Each state reached the frozen verdict validated and useful: an area under the ROC curve above the frozen usefulness bar and above a climatology baseline, with intervals. Per-case probabilities and regime-stratified verification remain shown for the three pseudo-regimes that drive the correction models.
rows.limitation: The labels are objective, rule-based and in the style of published methods; they are not the published classifications and not an expert analysis, and the percentile-based labels are relative by construction. Skill was shown on three held-out reforecast seasons of control-member forecasts, not on other operational years and not on a new cycle. The correction models still route on the earlier forecast-only pseudo-regimes, whose class named Active was found not to match observed active spells (docs/136); this detection model is a separate classifier. Regime-awareness was not shown to improve the heavy-rain correction on the sealed years.

rows.summary: Rule-based coastal and orographic geographic-forcing zones are defined, the frozen models are verified inside each zone, and a forecast-time forcing regime concentrates the observed Ghats-coast heavy rain on the development years. A forecast-time detector of Ghats-coast rain days (forcing index, regime features, lead and season) was fitted on 2000-2011 and tested once on the sealed years 2014-2016 against an IMD rain-day label: it reached the frozen verdict validated and useful.
rows.limitation: The label is an IMD rule (zone-mean rainfall in the upper range of the training years), relative by construction, not an expert analysis. The detector says whether a coastal or orographic rain day is likely, not how much rain falls: there is no specialist rainfall model for the zone, and the geography-aware correction experiments showed only a modest, one-year gain in Ghats-coast heavy-rain detection. Skill was shown on three held-out reforecast seasons, not on other operational years.

rows.summary: A forecast-time detector of western-disturbance presence (the forecast 500 hPa trough indicator, the other forecast regime features, lead and season) was fitted on 2000-2011, selected under a frozen protocol and tested once on the sealed years 2014-2016 against an objective ERA5 500 hPa vorticity label: it reached the frozen verdict validated and useful. The earlier indicator-only check on the operational years, which found no consistent association with rainfall, is kept and shown.
rows.limitation: The label is a rule on ERA5 geopotential in the style of published feature tracking, not the published tracker and not an expert analysis, and it is relative by construction. The task compares a forecast trough with a reanalysis trough, so it largely verifies the forecast height field; it is not a measure of rainfall skill, and the earlier operational-year check found no consistent link between the indicator and north-west India rainfall. The corpus covers June to early October, when these systems seldom act. No western-disturbance-aware correction model exists and the rainfall verification domain still stops where these systems act.

rows.requirement: Independent (expert / bulletin) validation of regime labels
rows.summary: The forecast-only pseudo-regimes are checked against observation-based rainfall criteria for active and break spells (IMD data, the style of Rajeevan et al. 2010, a 36-year climatology that shares no year with any evaluated population), under a protocol frozen before any score. Only the active task met the support gate, in two populations; the check found that the pseudo-class named Active does not correspond to observed active spells. A second check on a much longer independent record (2000-2016 reforecast, objective IMD and ERA5 labels, sealed years 2014-2016) found the detection tasks for active, break, low/depression, western disturbance and coastal rain days validated and useful.
rows.limitation: Partial by construction: active versus not active could be scored in two populations only, break versus not break in none, and depression is not validated. The labels are an implementation of rainfall criteria with documented deviations, not the published classification and not an expert review. In both scored populations the balanced accuracy is below the chance level, and most observed active days fall in the low/depression pseudo-class. The second check also uses objective rule-based labels and never an expert or bulletin analysis, so the row stays partial: expert-assigned regime labels remain unavailable.

rows.requirement: AI/ML post-processing of raw NWP rainfall
rows.summary: A frozen ladder of Raw, Ridge MOS, global gradient-boosted trees, hard regime-routed experts and a soft regime mixture is trained on earlier seasons and evaluated on later ones.
rows.limitation: Small training seasons; the extreme-rain tail is sparse; the models are frozen historical artifacts, not a live service.

rows.summary: Hard routing (M3) and a soft probability-weighted mixture (M4) correct rainfall with regime specialists; RMSE against Raw is shown for both tracks.
rows.limitation: Regime-aware models do not beat the global model on RMSE, MAE or bias. Their heavy-rain event skill gain appears on the operational-era track only, mainly in the Low / Depression regime, and does not appear on the 2019 reforecast track. On the sealed 2014-2016 reforecast years the regime-aware routing did not beat the non-regime model on heavy-rain skill or error, so regime-awareness is not shown to add value there.

rows.requirement: Improved rainfall forecast versus raw NWP, especially heavy and very heavy rain
rows.summary: The correction improves RMSE, heavy-rain CSI and very-heavy CSI over Raw, each with an interval excluding zero, in two independent reforecast tests: the sealed years 2014-2016 and a confirmatory test on 2017-2019 in which the frozen bundle (the event-weighted regression with a one-parameter mean-error correction, plus exceedance classifiers) meets the frozen verdict. On the operational-era track earlier corrections also improved heavy-rain detection on an independent year. The same frozen bundle is also shown on the 2019 cases of the maps and the district product, beside the global model, as a labelled descriptive layer (docs/143).
rows.limitation: In the first test the frozen mean-error guardrail failed (the correction over-forecast by roughly twice the limit) and the confirmatory pass depends on a mean-error shift read from that first test; the 2017-2019 years were used by earlier Track A experiments, so they are confirmatory and not untouched. The gain is for the reforecast control member (a different model version from the operational years, never pooled with them), not for operational forecasts of other years or a new cycle. Very-heavy detection comes from exceedance classifiers (yes/no forecasts at a fixed probability threshold, not shown to be calibrated), not from the corrected rainfall field. Regime-awareness was not shown to add value over the non-regime model, and the frozen regime-aware models of the operational years still have mixed heavy-rain skill. The product layer covers the 2019 reforecast cases only, shows scores and a yes/no forecast that over-forecasts events, and is not applied to the operational years.

rows.summary: District-event and district-mean verification under protocols frozen before any result, for both tracks: the 2017-2019 reforecast track (2018 development, 2019 post-hoc) and the operational-era track (2024 development, 2025 post-hoc). Track A carries every definition over unchanged from the Track B protocol.
rows.limitation: Aggregate verification of historical replay, not warning skill, with optimistic intervals; the two tracks are never pooled. District-mean error against Raw improves for every corrected model on the 2017-2019 reforecast track in both years and on the operational-era track in 2025, but in 2024 it improves only slightly for the Ridge and global models and is worse than Raw for the two regime-aware models. District heavy-rain event detection of the corrected models on the 2019 reforecast track is below Raw's.

rows.summary: A separate worker takes one NOAA GEFS 00 UTC cycle, applies the canonical rainfall quality control and the frozen operational-era models without retraining, and publishes an immutable, hash-manifested bundle that a read-only API and an Experimental Live Cycle page serve with an experimental, unverified label. The worker path reproduces the frozen 2025 outputs exactly on stored cycles, and refuses broken inputs.
rows.limitation: No skill can be shown for a new cycle until observations exist, so every live product is labelled experimental and unverified and is not an official warning. The repository carries no live bundle: whether one has been fetched and published is shown on the page, not assumed here. There is no scheduler, retry, alerting or hosted worker, and the input is NOAA GEFS, not an NCMRWF model. The frozen models may extrapolate if the GEFS configuration drifts, which the applicability check only flags as a range heuristic. Only the control member is used and no district table is produced for a live cycle.

rows.requirement: Synoptic meteorology overlays (wind vectors, geopotential contours, pressure isobars)
rows.summary: A synoptic chart of the wide forecast domain draws 850-hPa wind arrows, 500-hPa geopotential height contours and sea-level pressure isobars over shaded precipitable water or 700-hPa humidity, on a map with a basemap, with a rainfall-domain outline and an exact point reader. Every layer is built from the frozen forecast fields.
rows.limitation: Operational-era track only (the 2019 reforecast track has no wide-domain chart in the app). One forecast snapshot per case at the case's own lead, no animation. The fields are the control-member forecast, not an analysis, and the chart is not a causal explanation of any correction.

rows.summary: The unmodified Raw GEFS control rainfall is verified against IMD over the whole IMD grid, by region, with the error, bias and heavy-rain skill of each region and confidence intervals. The correction models themselves are still restricted to the regional window over peninsular and central India.
rows.limitation: Raw only: no model was applied or trained outside the regional window, so there is no corrected all-India forecast and nothing is known about how a correction would behave in the north, the east or the north-east. The wider reconstruction excluded further cases, so the populations are smaller than the regional study. Raw has little heavy-rain skill in every region and a wet bias in the east and north-east, so a correction trained in the window would not simply transfer. Each additional region needs its own corpus version, district weights and observation coverage check.
